name: Swarm
why: How many agents coordinated on shared pages and channels, as a question asks it: a row per account (or per name its saves sign with), columns in event order, and as cards the records the labels that are on mark, coloured by value, with the links the records carry (replies, names of other accounts, the save before on the same place); a question typed in the page goes to the analyst's Claude Code session, which answers it with labels the chart then draws.
data: A survey team's shared wiki and chat over one night, and its roster. roster.csv: `account`, `objective` and `joined`. wiki/index.jsonl: the pages (`slug`, `title`, `created`, `by`). wiki/pages/<slug>.jsonl: one page's saves (`rev`, `user` or `ip`, `ts`, `summary`, `text`, the whole page after the save). chat/<channel>.jsonl: posts (`id`, `channel`, `user`, `ts`, `text`, `reply_to`) and join notices; night-ops.jsonl is in a later export's fields (`room`, `author`, `sent` in epoch milliseconds, `body`, `parent`). The reader finds each file's fields by name, compares each save with the one before it on its page, and draws as cards what the labels that are on mark. It handles times in ISO 8601 with Z or an offset, with a space and no zone, and in epoch seconds or milliseconds; a post with no time; a replayed save and a post delivered twice; posts logged out of order; a torn last line (the page reports it with any other line that does not parse); a roster that capitalises an account differently, leaves objectives empty and runs one over two lines; a save by an address with no account; and a save that changes only whitespace.

accepts.means: the record on line <n>: its card when the chart shows it, else the record beside the chart; a roster row opens its account

declares.means: one account: its row, its goal and all its records
one page or channel, such as place/Night-14/Schedule: all its records
